question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $64u+28v=\text{gcd}(64,28).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}64 & = & 28\cdot 2 & + & 8 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 28 & = & 8\cdot 3 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 8 & = & 4\cdot 2 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(64,28)=4.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =64-28\cdot 2 \\ 4 & =28-8\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =28-8\cdot 3 \\  & =28-(64-28\cdot 2)\cdot 3 \\  & =28\cdot 7-64\cdot 3 \\  & =64\cdot (-3)+28\cdot 7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-3)+7=4.
$$
